question: Do you need a reason to live?

lines.text: Do you need a reason to live? Two philosophers. You pick a side.
Yes. Man is a reed that knows it will die. So we run to games, gossip, scrolling. I call it diversion. Only an infinite reason fills an infinite hole.
His claim: without a reason, life is just distraction from death.
We demand meaning. The universe stays silent. That clash is the absurd. Don't escape it. Live inside it, eyes open.
His claim: there's no reason coming. Live anyway, without excuses.
You're already on the boat. Refuse to bet, and you've bet. Stake one finite life, win infinity. Only a fool passes.
Your wager is philosophical suicide. You kill the question to feel safe. Sisyphus has no hope, and still, the struggle itself is enough to fill a heart.
lines.say: Your wager is philosophical... You kill the question to feel safe. Sisyphus has no hope, and still, the struggle itself is enough to fill a heart.

lines.text: He says not betting is losing. But hope is just one more diversion. Point, Camus.
Then forget proof. The heart has reasons reason cannot know.
Passion with no proof. That's the absurd hero.
Pascal dropped proof to stay in the fight. That's Camus's rule. Camus wins.
So keep both. From Pascal: notice what you reach for when it's quiet. From Camus: you don't need an answer to push the rock. Stop running. Keep pushing.
Which brings you back to the question.
